notes: Sender: the pushbutton sits across columns 5 and 7 of the breadboard. The black wire takes GND to column 5 and the yellow wire takes D2 to column 7. The sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP, so no external resistor is used.

Receiver: the LED cathode (straight leg) is in column 6, where the black GND wire lands. The LED anode (bent, longer leg) is in column 8 and meets resistor leg 1. Resistor leg 2 is in column 11, where the green wire from D2 lands.
The diagram's breadboard labels its top half f-j and its bottom half a-e. The catalogue calls the f-j half bank 'b', so the holes are written as e.g. '5b.f'.
The diagram shows only two pushbutton legs. I used 1.l and 2.l, one on each side of the switch.
The LED resistor value is not given in the tutorial. 220 ohm is assumed.
The antenna's cable to the board's u.FL connector is modelled as a direct joined and electrical edge between the antenna and the board's ANT port.
USB cables are in the parts list but not drawn in the diagrams. Each is joined to its board's USB port, and the PC end is not modelled.
